events.title: Columbus Departs from Palos on First Voyage
events.description: Christopher Columbus set sail from Palos de la Frontera, Spain, with the Santa María, Pinta, and Niña, seeking a western sea route to Asia under the sponsorship of the Spanish crown.
events.significance: The voyage led to the first sustained European contact with the Americas, profoundly reshaping world history, trade, and demographics.

events.title: Germany Declares War on France
events.description: Germany declared war on France at the start of World War I, following its earlier declaration against Russia, and invaded Belgium the same day as part of the Schlieffen Plan.
events.significance: The declaration widened the conflict into a continental war, and the invasion of Belgium prompted Britain to enter the war on August 4.

Jesse Owens Wins First Gold Medal at Berlin Olympics
events.description: American sprinter Jesse Owens won the 100-meter dash at the 1936 Berlin Summer Olympics, the first of four gold medals he would win at the Games.
events.significance: Owens' victories challenged Nazi claims of Aryan racial superiority and made him one of the most celebrated athletes in history.

events.title: USS Nautilus Reaches the North Pole
events.description: The US Navy nuclear-powered submarine USS Nautilus became the first vessel to reach the geographic North Pole, traveling beneath the Arctic ice cap.
events.significance: The feat demonstrated the capabilities of nuclear propulsion and had major strategic implications during the Cold War.
